title: Tab reaches every card, row and header in on-screen order with a focus ring
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Reach") has four Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17701) and {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17702) led by {Technician-A}, {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17703) led by {Technician-B}, and {Work-order-4} (for example S10043-17704) with no lead technician.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Click once in the Search box, then put the mouse aside: from here on use only the keyboard.
  5. Press Tab repeatedly until a card has focus, looking at the screen after each press.
  6. Keep pressing Tab and write down, in order, every card and column header that gets focus.
  7. Press Shift+Tab a few times and write down where focus goes.
  8. Click Tech View in the display switcher, click once in the Search box and put the mouse aside again.
  9. Press Tab repeatedly until a row has focus.
  10. Keep pressing Tab and write down, in order, every row and group header that gets focus.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 5: Tab reaches the cards, and the focused card shows a visible focus ring.
  • Step 6: Tab moves through the column headers and cards in on-screen order: column by column from left to right, and top to bottom within each column. Every card and every column header is reached. Tab also stops on controls inside a header or card (such as the pin or More actions button) on the way.
  • Step 7: Shift+Tab moves back through the same order.
  • Step 9: the focused row shows a visible focus ring.
  • Step 10: Tab moves through the group headers and rows from top to bottom. Every row and every group header is reached.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 54 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S11-R1, S11-R3 and the Story 11 user story, read 15 Oct 2026. title: A card's more-actions menu appears on hover or focus and offers Reassign
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 10 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011). A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • [User-A]: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • One technician at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location.
  • One Approved work order for that customer, [WO-1], led by [Tech-A].
  • Names and numbers are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm each technician below is active at this location with Time Clock on, or add it: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  3. Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" > Save (if it already exists, open it instead). On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, TRK-118) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" and its asset > Save. The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form open: in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; the build offers only ready-made lines), turn Line Approved on > Save & Close; the work order becomes Approved. Repeat for one work order only; record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702) (numbers on this site look like "S10043-17581").
  5. Set the leads: on an Approved work order pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned. Here: [WO-1] = [Tech-A].
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu — [WO-1] shows, led by [Tech-A]. If not, set the lead before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu so only this test's work orders show.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  5. Hover the [WO-1] card.
  6. Click the more-actions button (three dots) that appears.
  7. Read the menu items.
  8. Press Escape and move the mouse off the card.
  9. Press Tab repeatedly until the [WO-1] card (or a control inside it) has keyboard focus.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Hovering the card shows the more-actions button over the card.
  • The menu includes the Reassign lead technician action. The design labels it "Reassign Lead Tech" ("Assign Tech" on a card with no lead): write down the label you see, a different label alone is not a fail.
  • When the card gets keyboard focus, the more-actions button shows without hovering.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-R13, S3-R14, read 8 Oct 2026. Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Dana Delete) is a new staff member made for this case only, active at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and the Technician role, with no labor recorded on any work order, because this test deletes them.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Deleted Lead") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17901) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Read the header of the column that holds {Work-order-1}.
  4. Click your initials (top right) and open Settings > Staff.
  5. Click the pencil icon on {Technician-A}.
  6. Click Delete and confirm the deletion.
  7. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click List in the display switcher.
  8. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  9. Read the Lead Technician of {Work-order-1} and write it down.
  10. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  11. Find {Work-order-1} and read the header of the column that holds it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: {Work-order-1} is in a column headed with {Technician-A}'s name.
  • Step 11: {Work-order-1} is not in a column headed "Unknown Technician". Every column header on the board names whose column it is.
  • Step 11: if {Work-order-1} is still in a technician's column, that column's header shows the same name as the Lead Technician you wrote down at step 9.

Known problem (SV-11416, open: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11416): today, at step 11, {Work-order-1} sits in a column headed "Unknown Technician" with a generic person icon. The deleted technician's name is not shown and the column has no inactive marker.

1. If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new.

2. If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it.

3. If it passes, the fix has shipped: tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 58 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R11b and S3-R3, with S3-N2, S3-N4 and the Decisions entry of 2026-09-13 as the nearest rules, read 16 Oct 2026. Defect SV-11416 (open). Source-verified 16 October 2026.

The spec says what happens when a lead technician is deactivated (the work stays in their column, marked inactive, so it stays attributable) but not when the technician is deleted. SV-11416 asks the product owner to decide: show the technician's name with the inactive marker, as for a deactivated technician, or move the work order to Unassigned.
